subtopics.title: Slope Aspect — Which Side Gets the Sun

questions.question: Slope aspect is defined as:
options: The steepness of a slope
The direction a slope faces
The height of a slope above sea level
The vegetation cover on a slope

questions.question: In the Southern Hemisphere, north-facing slopes are warmer because:
options: They are closer to the equator in distance
They receive more rainfall
The midday sun stands in the northern sky, so its rays strike them at a high, concentrated angle for more hours
They are sheltered from all wind

questions.question: Which description fits the SOUTH-facing slope of a South African east-west valley?
options: Cooler and damper, with denser green vegetation and snow lying longest
Drier soil, sparse grass and early snowmelt
The preferred slope for vineyards and table grapes
The warmest slope in the valley

questions.question: Aspect contrasts between valley walls are greatest:
options: In summer, in north-south valleys
At midday on the equator
During thunderstorms
In winter, in east-west valleys, when the sun is lowest

subtopics.title: The Valley's Daily Breathing — Anabatic and Katabatic Winds

questions.question: An anabatic wind is:
options: A night-time downslope drainage of cold air
A hot dry wind off the plateau
A daytime upslope breeze driven by heated valley sides
A regional wind blowing along the valley

questions.question: Katabatic winds form at night because air touching the radiating slopes:
options: Chills, becomes denser and slides downhill under gravity
Warms and rises
Is pushed down by the jet stream
Expands and floats away

questions.question: Katabatic drainage is strongest on:
options: Cloudy, windy summer nights
Clear, calm winter nights when radiation loss is fastest
Hot afternoons
Rainy mornings

questions.question: The cold air carried by katabatic winds finally:
options: Escapes over the ridge
Rises to form afternoon cumulus
Warms as it descends and disappears
Pools on the valley floor like water filling a basin

subtopics.title: Night in the Valley — Inversion, Thermal Belt, Frost and Fog

questions.question: A valley temperature inversion means that at night:
options: Temperature increases with height above the valley floor — the normal pattern is upside down
Temperature falls steadily with height
The valley floor is the warmest place
All levels have the same temperature

questions.question: The thermal belt is:
options: The coldest zone on the valley floor
The zone of strongest wind on the ridge
The warm mid-slope zone sitting above the ponded cold air and below the cooling upper slopes
A band of thunderstorms along the valley

questions.question: Radiation fog forms on the valley floor when:
options: Warm rain falls into cold air
The anabatic wind carries moisture upslope
Smoke mixes with cloud
The ponded moist air is cooled to its dew point by radiative cooling

questions.question: Valley towns wear a grey blanket of smoke on winter mornings because:
options: The wind blows smoke in from the coast
The inversion's warm lid traps smoke and dust in the cold air below it
Fires burn more fuel in winter only
Fog turns grey at sunrise

subtopics.title: People in the Valley — Farming, Settlement and Sensible Planning

questions.question: Frost-sensitive orchards and vineyards are planted on the mid-slope because:
options: The soil is deepest there
It is closest to the river
The thermal belt keeps the mid-slope frost-free on clear winter nights
Land is cheapest there

questions.question: Wind machines and orchard heaters fight frost by:
options: Stirring the inversion's warm upper air down into the orchard and warming the cold surface layer
Blowing the frost off the leaves
Drying the soil
Creating anabatic winds

questions.question: Locating informal settlements on valley-floor land is a planning failure because the floor is:
options: Too steep to build on
Too far from rivers
Always rocky
The coldest, foggiest, most flood-prone and most smoke-trapped zone in the valley

questions.question: Winter fog warnings and freeway pile-ups concentrate on low-lying road stretches because:
options: Roads follow the flat valley floors where radiation fog pools
Drivers speed up downhill
Fog only forms over tar
Roads on ridges are always closed

subtopics.title: The Sunny Wall and the Shady Wall

questions.question: The palm-flat versus palm-edge-on picture explains:
options: Why steep slopes erode faster
Why a slope facing the sun receives concentrated energy while one leaning away receives a skimming, diluted beam
Why valleys are windy
Why frost forms on metal

questions.question: In a South African east-west valley, the braai side — warm, dry, vine-covered — is the:
options: South-facing wall
Valley floor
North-facing wall
Ridge top

questions.question: If the same valley were in Europe, the warm wall would be:
options: The south-facing wall, because the Northern Hemisphere midday sun stands in the southern sky
Still the north-facing wall
Neither wall
Both walls equally

subtopics.title: The Bathtub That Fills With Cold Air

questions.question: In the bathtub picture, the two taps filling the tub are:
options: Rain and rivers
The anabatic winds of both walls
Fog and frost
The katabatic drainage flowing down both valley walls at night

questions.question: The memory anchor for the two valley winds is:
options: Anabatic ascends; katabatic collapses downhill
Anabatic arrives at night; katabatic comes at noon
Both winds blow along the valley
Katabatic climbs; anabatic drains

questions.question: The little cauliflower clouds on the peaks by afternoon are made by:
options: Katabatic winds cooling the summit
Anabatic winds pumping warm air up the slopes all day
The inversion lifting
Radiation fog rising from the floor

questions.question: By three in the morning, the full bathtub means the temperatures in the valley run:
options: Warmest at the floor, coldest at the rim
The same at all heights
Coldest at the floor with warmer air floating above — an inversion
Coldest at the ridge tops only

subtopics.title: Frost on the Floor, Money on the Shelf

questions.question: The frost pocket is the bathtub turned freezer — it forms where:
options: Ponded cold air in a hollow or valley floor chills below zero on a clear night
Snow falls on the ridge
The anabatic wind blows strongest
The thermal belt overheats

questions.question: In the Hex River valley, orchards and vineyards stripe the mid-slope because that is:
options: Where the river floods
The only flat land available
The foggiest zone
The thermal belt — above the frost bath, below the cold heights

questions.question: A helicopter hovering over orchard blocks on a critical frost night works because it:
options: Blows the blossoms off before they freeze
Stirs the warm inversion air down into the cold surface layer, like stirring the bathtub
Dries the orchard with its downdraft
Scares birds away from the fruit

questions.question: Sensible valley planning places:
options: Housing on the floor and orchards on the ridge
Industry in the valley bottom
Homes on the thermal belt, smoky industry out of the inversion pond, and fields and parks on the floor
Everything on the south-facing wall
